messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — starting ~08:40 UTC I'm seeing intermittent tail latency spikes for hosted eu-west inference (p50 fine, p99 up to +400ms). Graphs show narrow windows aligned with rack A3 thermal throttle and ToR interface drops. link: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west/gpu-latency
Aj Patel: I noticed the same on our dedicated tenant slice in eu-west-1b. Throughput stayed steady but there are short PCIe retransmit counters and a couple of NIC CRC errors. Could be ToR flapping + powercap interaction.
Kevin Zhou: Any pod-evictions or preemptions around that time? Might be noisy burst + slot migration causing cache churn.
Maria Chen: No pod evictions in the logs. Noisy bursts look tenant-driven — some clients hit warm-pool + burst at approx the same time. But the timing lines up with a PDU powercap kick in A3 per infra telemetry.
Linh Tran: @sre-bot did we have any automated thermal throttle actions in A3?
sre-bot: Alert: rack-A3 thermal threshold exceeded at 08:39:12 UTC. Action: initiated powercap reduction to 85% for 90s.
Aj Patel: That matches. Powercap + ToR retransmits could cause packet queuing and stall the NVLink/PCIe traffic briefly, which would spike token latency even if GPU utilization looks normal.
Kevin Zhou: Suggestion: route dedicated bursty tenants off A3 racks temporarily and shadow-redirect a small fraction to eu-west-1a warm-pool to validate. Also capture tcpdump on ToR-facing NICs for the window.
Maria Chen: Good call. I'll open a quick canary reroute for 5% of the affected tenant traffic. Can we get a short-lived flow capture?
Linh Tran: Ops-automations can spin up a mirror session. @ops-automations run mirror for rack-A3 duration 08:38-08:46 UTC and put pcap in /tmp/maria-a3-0838.pcap
ops-automations: Mirror session created, storing pcap to s3://infra-dumps/maria-a3-0838.pcap
Aj Patel: Also dump kernel NIC stats and nvlink counters from nodes in the rack: /var/log/kernel/netstats.log and /var/log/gpu/nvlink.log for the timeframe.
Maria Chen: Collected and uploaded logs to the incident folder. link: https://s3.redwood/incident/1799502468/logs
Kevin Zhou: If reroute reduces spikes, it's likely ToR/powercap combo. If not, follow-up: check scheduler's slot reassignment for cross-socket NUMA penalties and KVCACHE misses.
Linh Tran: I'll coordinate with networking to check switch counters and backlog. If confirmed, we should add a short-term routing rule to avoid racks that recently had powercap events for 10m after event. Could be a cheap isolation guardrail.
Maria Chen: Agreed. For now canary reroute is live. Monitoring p99 and ToR drop counters.
Aj Patel: FYI cost note — pushing traffic to warm-pools temporarily will marginally increase GPU-hours and egress; we should keep the canary small (<=10%).
Maria Chen: Can we keep this thread for updates? Will post final conclusions and a PR for the routing guardrail if we confirm. :thumbsup:
Linh Tran: ack, keeping an eye.
Kevin Zhou: ack.
Maria Chen: Final update: after reroute p99 dropped back to normal within 2 minutes, ToR retransmits decreased. Plan: short-term routing guardrail + ops to check PDU firmware schedule. I'll file follow-up playbook and a small scheduler tweak PR.
Aj Patel: Thanks, filing the cost impact note in the ticket.
Linh Tran: Noted. Closing monitoring loop and adding runbook step for 'avoid recent powercap racks'
Maria Chen: closing thread after runbook PR merged.
